Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

argument noun

reasons given for a view

also a good argument, line of argument, argue that, put forward an argument

classical

Cic. Top. 8: argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem

argūmentum, argūmentī n.

noun, second declension

an argument, a proof

Lewis & Short: an argument resting chiefly on facts, where ratiō rests on reasoning. Also the plot of a play or a story (see subject).

Other words

  • argūmentor, argūmentārī, argūmentātus sum — argue, bring arguments

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 3.9: sī quid est ēvidēns, dē quō inter omnīs conveniat, argūmentārī

    To argue that something is so, with an accusative and infinitive: contendere (see claim).

Examples

  • itaque licet dēfīnīre locum esse argūmentī sēdem, argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem

    so we may define a topic as the home of an argument, and an argument as reasoning that makes a doubtful point believableCic. Top. 8

See also argument, reason, conclusion, debate.
